According to the prosecution case, the respondent no.2 lodged an FIR on the allegations that she got married to Kuldeep Parashar on 3.3.2020. The respondent no.2 is an educated lady and is a Software Engineer and is working in CGI Company at Bangalore. Kuldeep Parashar was also working in the same company; whereas applicants no.5 and 6 namely; Prashant Vajpayi and Smt.Priyanka Vajpayi were also working in SAP Company at Bangalore. During the discussions for marriage, the applicants no.1, 2, 3 and 4 expressed that the talks of marriage of Kuldeep Parashar is going on at some different place, where an offer has been made to give Rs.10,00,000/- and a big car apart from the household articles, therefore, the parents of the respondent no.2 should also give the same dowry in the marriage. Accordingly, it was alleged that the parents of the respondent no.2 had given Rs.10,00,000/- in cash, gold chain of 2 tola, gold neckless of 2 tola, gold earring, etc. and also gave the household articles like fridge, washing machine, double bed, dressing table, sitting table, water purifier, kitchen set, steel utensils etc.,worth Rs.3,50,000/-. The details of the total jewellery given at the time of marriage etc. and the other gifts were also mentioned in the FIR. While they were returning back after the marriage was performed, they stopped at a hotel for having food where the applicants no.1 and 3 were discussing that they were expecting a big car, which has not been given. She stayed in her matrimonial house for 7 days and during this period, the applicants no.1 to 4 suggested to the respondent no.2 that it would not be proper to keep so much of jewellery in Bangalore because both of them are working , therefore, the respondent no.2 should leave her ornaments with the applicants no.1 to 4 and whenever she would ask for the same, the jewellery would be returned back. Even the applicants no.5 and 6 also assured that the jewellery would be returned as soon as it is required. Therefore, by relying upon the assurance given by the applicants, the respondent no.2 left her jewellery with applicants no.1 to 4. Thereafter, the respondent no.2 and her husband came to Gadarwara on the festival of Holi and the applicants no.1 to 4 also came to Gadarwara and they resided there for 2 days. During this period it was alleged by the applicants no.1 to 4 that the respondent no.2 has not handed over the entire jewellery and since they would be residing in Bangalore, therefore, the respondent no.2 must handover the entire jewellery, which would be in the safe custody of the applicants. Accordingly, with an assurance to return the jewellery, the applicants no.1 to 4 took the entire gold ornaments from the respondent no.2. When the respondent no.2 went to Bangalore then it is alleged that her husband started alleging that they would be required to stay in a rented house and since he has no money for payment of advance and earnest money, therefore, the respondent no.2 should take a house on rent and accordingly, the respondent no.2 paid Rs.2,00,000/- towards the advance rent and the earnest money and also purchased the household articles worth Rs.5,00,000/-. After the rented house was taken, the behavior of Kuldeep Parashar changed all of sudden and started alleging that the wish of his family members was that they would get a big car, but a big car has not been given and dowry as per their wishes, has also not been given. When it was objected by the respondent no.2 that her parents have already given sufficient dowry as per their financial capabilities, then her husband started quarrelling with her and also assaulted her and alleged and unless and until a big car is given, he will not keep her with him and he was also not visiting the house in the night. When this fact was informed by the respondent no.2 to applicants on phone and told about her difficulties then all of them stated that since her parents have not given the dowry, as per the wishes of in-laws and has also not given the big car, therefore, she should take a big car from her parent, otherwise she is free to take divorce and thereafter the in-laws stopped talking to the respondent no.2. The husband of the respondent no.2 got the locks of the house changed and kept the key with him and on one day Jagdish Parashar vs The Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184044456/ 3 the respondent no.2 was made to wait for 4 to 5 hours. Even her husband did not bring the key and under compulsion the respondent no.2 was compelled to go to house of her sister. They stayed in the rented house for 2 months and during this period, her husband was consistently quarrelling with her and was insisting that she should go back to her parental house and should fulfill the demands, otherwise he would perform second marriage and in case if any objection is raised, then she would be killed. They are the residents of UP and nobody would be able to find out the whereabouts of her dead body also. On 28.6.2020 her husband vacated the house in her absence and shifted to Lalitpur along with the entire household articles and since then he has no contact with the respondent no.2. With great difficulty the respondent no.2 succeeded in talking to her husband then he specifically narrated that their intention was to extort the money from them and they have successfully done so and, therefore, the respondent no.2 may do whatever she wants. Although the respondent no.2 gave an information of this incident to the police but since she was not interested in severing the marital ties, therefore, she did not narrate the incidents in detail. It was alleged that her parents are not in a position to give a big car; whereas her husband and her in-laws are demanding dowry. They are again and again are sending messages to the relatives that either their demand should be fulfilled; otherwise they have already deserted the respondent no.2. During her stay in her parental home, the applicants are harassing her mentally and she has an apprehension that they would permanently severe the relationship and accordingly an FIR was lodged. Delay in lodging the FIR 8. According to the respondent no.2, the marriage was performed on 4.3.2020 and her husband deserted her permanently on 28.6.2020; whereas the FIR was lodged with delay of 8 months.
texts.arguments: The allegations, which have been made against the applicants, are vague, omnibus and general in nature and in the light of judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Kans Raj v. State of Punjab, reported in (2000) 5 SCC 207, Monju Roy v. State of W.B., (2015) 13 SCC 693, Chandralekha & Ors. v. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2013 (1) UC 155, Geeta Mehrotra Vs. State of U.P. reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741, Preeti Gupta Vs. State of Jharkhand, reported in (2010) 7 SCC 667, the prosecution of the applicants is unwarranted. Even if the entire allegations are read, no offence under sections 498- A, 506-II and 406 of IPC is made out. In reply, it is submitted by counsel for the applicants that merely because the charges have been framed, it would not mean that the application for quashment of proceedings would become Jagdish Parashar vs The Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184044456/ 4 infructuous.

9. The moot question for consideration is as to whether the FIR, which was lodged after a delay of 8 months, can be said to be bad, warranting the quashment of the proceedings as well as the FIR or not?
10. As per the provisions of section 468 of CrPC, the period of limitation for taking cognizance is 3 years.
The respondent no.2 was permanently deserted by her husband on 28.6.2020; whereas the FIR was lodged on 22.5.2021.
Thus, it is clear that the FIR was lodged much within a period of 3 years and thus, it cannot be said that it is barred by time.
11. Furthermore, it is clear from the FIR that the respondent no.2 has been compelled to live separately on account of non-fulfillment of demand of dowry.
Compelling a woman to live separately on account of non-fulfillment of demand of dowry would certainly amount to cruelty.

The impact on the mental health of the wife by overt acts on the part of the husband or his relatives; the mental stress and trauma of being driven away from the matrimonial home and her helplessness to go back to the same home for fear of

The emotional distress or psychological effect on the wife, if not the physical injury, is bound to continue to traumatise the wife even after she leaves the matrimonial home and takes shelter at the parental home.

Even if the acts of physical cruelty committed in the matrimonial house may have ceased and such acts do not occur at the parental home,
there can be no doubt that the mental trauma and the psychological distress caused by the acts of the h

Mental cruelty borne out of physical cruelty or abusive and humiliating verbal exchanges would continue in the parental home even though there may not be any overt act of physical cruelty at such place."

15. The Supreme Court in the case of Skoda Auto Volkswagen (India) Private Limited. v. State of U.P. and others, reported in (2021) 5 SCC 95 has held that in a petition for quashing the FIR, the Court cannot go into disputed question of fac
The mere delay on the part of complainant in lodging the complaint cannot by itself be a ground to quash the FIR.
The Court cannot embark upon an enquiry as to the reliability, correctness of the allegations made in FIR or in complaint and criminal proceedings can not be scuttled at initial stage.

16. The Supreme Court in the case of Ravinder Kumar and another v. State of Punjab, reported in (2001) 7 SCC 690 has held that attack on prosecution cases on the ground of delay in lodging FIR has almost bogged down as a stereotyped redunda
It is a recurring feature in most of the criminal cases that there would be some delay in furnishing the first information to the police.
It has to be remembered that law has not fixed any time for lodging the FIR.
Hence a delayed FIR is not illegal.

Of course, a prompt and immediate lodging of FIR is ideal as that would give the prosecution a twin advantage i.e. firstly it affords commencement of the investigation without any time lapse and secondly that it expels the opportunity for a
Even otherwise promptly lodged FIR is also not an unreserved guarantee for the genuineness of the version incorporated therein.
There may be variety of genuine causes for FIR lodgement to get delayed.

17. The Supreme Court in the case of Mohammad Wajid and another vs. State of U.P. and others,
reported in AIR 2023 SC 3784 has held that delay in registration of FIR, by itself cannot be a ground for quashing of FIR.
18. Thus, it is clear that not only there is no delay in lodging the FIR, but even otherwise the delay by itself cannot be ground to quash the proceedings.

Only the husband, his parents or at best close family members may be expected to demand dowry or to harass the wife but not distant relations, unless there is tangible material to support allegations made against such distant relations.

14.
From a reading of the complaint, it cannot be held that even if the allegations are taken as proved no case is made out.
There are allegations against Respondent 2 and his parents for harassing the complainant which forced her to leave the matrimonial home.
Even now she continues to be separated from the matrimonial home as she apprehends lack of security and safety and proper environment in the matrimonial home.
The question whether the appellant has in fact been harassed and treated with cruelty is a matter of trial but at this stage, it cannot be said that no case is made out.
Thus, quashing of proceedings before the trial is not permissible."
